9.0.s.en: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

9.0.0.en: In the face of God's great work with him, in rescuing him from death and his joy in marrying Sara, Tobias felt that all this was thanks to the guidance of the young man Azarias, and he sensed that his tongue could not express the measure of his thanks to him. So Tobias possessed the virtue of gratitude. He was also a humble man, and this is clear from his saying to the angel: If I became your slave, I would not repay your love and your care for me.

9.1.0.en: With the boldness of love, Tobias ventured to ask Azarias, making use of the time, to go to Rages, the large city near them, and to collect the silver from Gabael and give him the bond, and also to invite him to attend the wedding joys.

9.2.0.en: Another virtue that Tobias possessed was esteem for the feelings of others, for he wished not to be late for his parents, lest they be anxious at his delay, for anxiety assails aged parents.

9.3.0.en: On the other hand, Tobias esteemed the feelings of his father-in-law Raguel, who wanted him to stay two weeks with him to rejoice in his marriage. So he is an example of the spiritual man full of virtues.

9.3.1.en: Do you thank others for all that they offer you, and express by every means your appreciation for any work they do with you, however small? May you be humble, so that you feel the kindness of others toward you, especially the members of your household, even if their anxiety appears in a rebuke or reproach to you, for this springs from their love and attachment to you. Apologize to them and promise them that you will care for their feelings, and offer them more love, for love is the greatest thing in existence.

9.4.0.en: In great love Azarias responded to Tobias's request and prepared himself for the journey with four servants and two camels. He reached Rages and met Gabael, collected the silver from him and gave him the bond. Here God's care appears, in that Gabael had passed his financial crisis and was able to return all the money to its owner. Azarias here is a type of the spiritual man, striving on his journey in the wilderness of this world. He took two camels with him, and the camel here represents endurance of weariness in travel (striving). Two camels point to both inner striving and outer striving, and to confirm the importance of striving. Four servants point to the striving against the warfare of the devil, which comes from all four corners of the earth, that is, all kinds of warfare. When he completed his striving, he achieved his goal, which was the collecting of the money from Gabael, as the striver wins the Kingdom and the eternal inheritance.

9.4.1.en: Some of the Fathers see that Azarias, or the angel Raphael, is a type of the Holy Spirit, and the four rams are a type of the four Gospels, and the two camels are a type of the Apostles and the evangelists. The angel Raphael preached to Gabael and told him all that he had been commanded by Tobias, who is a type of Christ.

9.4.2.en: How beautiful is the cooperation between the two companions! They are an example for every two friends or companions who work or serve together: how they cooperate to achieve their goals, without thinking of the amount of weariness they have borne, and hurry together to the required work. Even if one of the two companions is the elder and greater, in humility he accepts to do any work however lowly: here the archangel hurries to collect the money for Tobias, though he is far above all these passing material works. It is love mingled with humility that drives to cooperation.

9.5.0.en: When Gabael learned the good news concerning Tobias and his marriage, he hurried with Azarias to congratulate him. Gabael embraced Tobias, who rushed toward him as soon as he entered. Gabael's feelings toward Tobit the father and his son appeared in his tears when he embraced Tobias. So Gabael too possessed the virtue of gratitude and appreciation for the love of Tobit the father, who had stood with him in his financial crisis; therefore he hurried to congratulate his son. Thus the members of the house of Raguel and the neighbors attended the wedding feast, and they are a type of the Jews who believed in Christ and partook of His Body and Blood. As for Gabael, he is a type of the distant Gentiles, like the Magi and all who believed in Christ from among the Gentiles and enjoyed the Holy Sacraments.

9.6.s.en: (2) The prayer of blessing offered by Gabael

9.6.0.en: Gabael asked the blessing of God, who is concerned for His people and His children (the God of Israel), and the reason for the blessing is the goodness and virtues of Tobit the father, for the blessing of fathers comes upon the children, and the children can make use of this blessing and increase in piety, so that greater blessings come upon them. They may also not benefit from it, but it becomes a cause of their judgment, if they do not walk uprightly.

9.7.0.en: And he asked God to pour out His blessing on Sara also, and on the parents Raguel and Anna, and also Tobit the father and his wife Anna.

9.8.0.en: He even asked a blessing for the children whom he hoped God would give to Tobias, and even the children's children and the offspring extending through the years. The birth of sons, as we mentioned, was a great blessing, because everyone was awaiting the birth of the awaited Messiah from his offspring. All these blessings he asked from God, the King forever and ever, the Almighty, who is able to give a continual blessing; therefore the hearts of the children of God are at ease, because they are in the care of this great and loving God. All who were gathered answered Amen to this great prayer, wishing with Gabael all these blessings.

9.8.1.en: How beautiful it is to offer prayers and wishes of blessing for all those around us and to encourage them by them, so that they are filled with hope.

9.9.0.en: In expression of joy, everyone came forward to eat from the feast (the wedding feast), which extended throughout the two weeks that Tobias spent with Raguel after his marriage. Here the marks of the joys of the children of God appear: they are in the fear of God; they feel the presence of God in their midst, so they do not go to excess in displays of material joy, which is incompatible with the presence of God. The feast also is a symbol of the sacrament of Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord, in which the faithful rejoice, and which they receive with reverence, fear and great awe. The anxiety of Tobias's parents, and the farewell of Sara and Tobias

10.0.s.en: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

10.0.0.en: The feelings of fatherhood and motherhood appear in the waiting of Tobias's parents for him. When he was slow beyond the expected time of his return, because of his marriage and the wedding feasts that continued two weeks, his parents became anxious, and Tobit the father began to think what might be the reasons for his delay.

10.1.0.en: He said: Perhaps he is still looking for Gabael, or Gabael has died.

10.2.0.en: They went on: they remained and continued.

10.2.1.en: From the intensity of emotion and anxiety the parents wept.

10.3.0.en: Our posterity: our offspring who succeeds us and speaks of us after our death.

10.3.1.en: A woman is distinguished by her more intense emotion than a man, so the mother Anna expressed her tense emotions, because of her son's delay, with many tears and words that show the feelings of aged parents toward their only young son. She felt that her son was the light of her eyes and her husband's; for in his vitality as a young man he can move quickly and see many things and teach his parents what they cannot reach. He is the helper and aid to his aged parents, who are weak in movement, in meeting their needs. And as the ability of the old to move diminishes, along with their indifference to material things, the movement and accomplishments of the son become an extension of their life and a consolation to them. He is also their hope and the fulfiller of the hopes which they could not fulfill in their lifetime, and even when they think of their death, they see the life of their son and his children as an extension of their life on earth.

10.3.2.en: These are the feelings of parents who love their children; how much ought children to appreciate these feelings?

10.4.0.en: The mother began to regret sending their son on this mission, for with her anxiety at his delay and the possibility of losing him, she felt that his mere presence was entirely sufficient, and that they had no need of his journey or of collecting the money.

10.4.1.en: How beautiful it is for a person to be content with what he has and thank God for it, even if the fulfillment of some of what he wants is delayed.

10.5.0.en: Tobit the father tried to reassure his wife that their son would return safely and that the man accompanying him was trustworthy.

10.6.1.en: But the mother's anxiety dominated her, so she went out every day to look at the roads leading to Nineveh, in case her son might be coming by one of them. This shows that if a person yields to thoughts of anxiety, he does not benefit from the reassuring words of God, so he should take refuge in God by prayer, and He will lift the anxiety from him and reassure him.

10.7.1.en: Raguel, out of his love for his daughter and for Tobias her husband, tried to keep them, so that he and his wife might enjoy their presence with them for a longer period, after the two weeks of the joyful feasts. So he proposed a new idea to Tobias, which was that he send a messenger from himself to Tobit his father, that he and his wife might be reassured of the safety of their son and be told of his marriage.

10.7.2.en: Raguel here is a type of the disciples of Christ and all His loved ones, who wished that Christ would remain with them on earth, that they might see Him with their eyes, but He made clear to them that He must ascend to heaven, for this was better for them, that they might live by faith with the help of the Holy Spirit. And Tobias, as we have already said, is a type of Christ. As Tobias insisted on returning to his father, so Christ also insisted on completing the redemption and ascending to His Father in heaven.

10.7.3.en: As Tobias took Sara his bride with him to his father, so Christ prepared a place for His Church (His bride) and received those who believe in Him into Paradise.

10.8.0.en: But the younger Tobias knew the extent of his parents' attachment to him and their anxiety, because of their old age, so he refused gently, despite Raguel's great urging. This shows that although he esteemed the love of Raguel and his wife, he esteemed his responsibility for his parents and his respect for their feelings, even if their anxiety was excessive.

10.9.s.en: (3) Raguel bids farewell to Tobias and Sara

10.9.0.en: After Raguel's attempt to keep Tobias and Sara for a longer time failed, he was not troubled or angry, because his motive was only love and not clinging to his personal opinion. He gave him Sara his wife and half of his property in servants, maidservants and animals.

10.9.1.en: Tobias's return to his father after completing his mission is a type of the Son's return to sit at the right hand of His Father after completing the redemption, as Christ says: "I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father" (Jn 16:28).

10.10.0.en: As for Raguel, he bade them farewell with joy, wishing them the company of the angel of God on the road, until they reached Tobias's parents. Raguel and his wife wished to live until they should see the children of Tobias and Sara and rejoice in them. It is beautiful for a person to have a hope and expectation throughout his life. Then the parents kissed their daughter Sara and bade farewell to the couple and those with them, that they might go in peace. In proportion as a person asks for the help of God he finds it: as Tobit the father asked for his son the company of the angel of God on his journey, Raguel also asked the company of the angel of God for him on his return. God answered him, and it was indeed the archangel who accompanied him at every step and took care of him.

10.10.1.en: It is beautiful that Raguel calls the parents of Tobias parents to the couple, for after marriage the parents-in-law become parents.

10.10.2.en: May every husband and wife look upon their parents-in-law with a filial regard, hurrying to honor them and be subject to them in humility, while making excuses for them because of their old age, and in appreciation of their toil through the past years in bringing up the son or daughter, and see in the parents-in-law's care for one of them a care for the other, for the couple feel that they are one before God.

10.11.0.en: Then Raguel and Anna gave their last charge to their daughter the bride, that she might walk by it in her new life. It is a very important charge, with its five components, which every new wife should care for and with which the parents charge their daughter the new bride.

10.11.1.en: The first part of this charge is honoring the parents-in-law, because they have become parents. It is strange that they put the honoring of parents before the relationship with the husband, although the basic relationship is with the husband, and it is the most important thing; but honoring the parents gives a calm atmosphere to the new married life, and even increases their love and care for the couple, in addition to the fact that the parents, because of their old age, ought to be honored in the last of their days.

10.11.2.en: Then comes the second part of the charge, which is love for the husband, with whom she is united and with whom she has one life; oneness cannot be achieved except by self-giving, sacrificial love.

10.11.3.en: The third part of the charge is care for the upbringing and nurture of the children whom God will bestow upon them, and the ordering and strengthening of the bonds of love, and the arranging of the relationship of love among the children themselves and between them and their parents, so that the family is bound together by the bond of love; and here the wisdom and love of the mother appear. The fourth part of the charge is the management of the house, which includes providing all the material needs for the husband and children, and care, and offering all this in a gentle and cheerful manner, and trying to avoid any conflict among the members of the family.

10.11.4.en: Finally we come to the fifth and last part, which is that she keep herself blameless, that is, preserve herself from obvious, evident, stumbling faults, such as evil dispositions. What is meant here is not mere error, for there is no person without sin or blame, but it means the importance of spiritual striving in personal life, that a person may be devout before God, and not forget the salvation of his soul amid the responsibilities of life.

10.11.5.en: Sara, as we said, is a type of the Church, and her parents-in-law are a type of the Law and the books of the Old Testament with all that is in them, for Christ declared that He came "not to destroy, but to fulfil" (Mt 5:17). The husband is Christ, who began with love, and the Church returned love for love: "We love him, because he first loved us" (1 Jn 4:19). As for the children, they are the faithful, and the Church brings up her children and manages their affairs with all the activities and services in her, and keeps herself in purity, far from sin.

10.11.6.en: The arrival of Tobias at his parents and the healing of Tobit the father from blindness

11.0.s.en: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

11.0.0.en: Haran: a city between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates, lying northeast of Damascus at a distance of two hundred and eighty miles. It is a commercial city, and the meaning of its name is the road, since it lies on a trade route. Terah and his son Abraham sojourned in it before Abraham went to Canaan, and Jacob also lived in it twenty years, married in it and begot his sons.

11.0.1.en: Tobias and the angel reached Haran, which lies halfway on the road to Nineveh, on the eleventh day (see Map 2, p. 265).

11.0.2.en: It is noted on the map that Haran lies northwest of Nineveh, but it was a station on the road coming from Rages, and after it the traveler descends to the southeast to Nineveh. Tobias here is a type of those of the eleventh hour, who reached Tobit the father, that is, received salvation, and they are the Jews who were contemporaries of Christ and believed, though many had preceded them who died in the hope of the resurrection; he is also a type of the Gentiles far from the faith who believed in Christ.

11.1.0.en: Tobias wanted to hurry to see his parents to reassure them, and because the angel felt the parents' anxiety, he proposed to Tobias that he divide the caravan into two parts, that the two of them should hurry first (probably they rode a horse, or two), and the rest of the caravan would then follow them, which included Sara and the servants and maidservants (the household), whom he sometimes called the servants, and with them the cattle.

11.2.0.en: Tobias agreed, and then the angel reminded him to take with him a part of the gall of the fish, for he would need it.

11.2.1.en: Tobias's hurrying to reach his father is a type of Christ's ascension as the representative of all humanity, to prepare for His bride and His Church (Sara) a place, and to rejoice the heart of God the Father (Tobit the father). Tobias's escape from death and the salvation of Sara is a type of Christ's resurrection from the dead, offering redemption to His Church.

11.3.0.en: In her longing to see her son, who was late in arriving, Anna used to go out every day and sit on the top of a hill outside Nineveh overlooking the roads leading to the city, for from there she could look a long distance. She did not tire of waiting, because of her love for her son. So the souls that love God await His coming, and as the Apostle Paul says: "having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ" (Phil 1:23).

11.4.0.en: One day, while she was watching the road, she saw from afar a person approaching, resembling her son in his movement, and with a mother's instinct she was certain that he was her son, so she hurried to give the good news to her husband Tobit.

11.5.1.en: As they were approaching the house, the angel instructed Tobias what to do when he entered. He told him to offer worship and thanks to God, and then kiss his father. God is first in our life, in our afflictions and in our joy, and we ought to offer Him reverence with thanksgiving; these are the feelings of prayer, and after that, being filled with the grace of God and His love, we can express our love to our loved ones.

11.6.0.en: Anoint: from anointing, that is, smear.

11.6.1.en: Then he instructed him to put some of the gall of the fish on the eyes of Tobit the father, and his eyes would be opened and he would see everything and rejoice at seeing God.

11.6.2.en: The younger Tobias is a type of Christ and the gall a type of the sufferings He endured on the Cross for the salvation of humanity, while Tobit the father is a type of humanity, which received spiritual enlightenment in the sacrament of Baptism through the sufferings of Christ and His redemption, which the gall typifies.

11.7.0.en: Wagging its tail: moving its tail.

11.7.1.en: While they were speaking they came very near to the house, and the dog that had accompanied them on the journey ran ahead, wagging its tail, announcing its joy at returning to its home, and it was like a herald to Tobit and his wife of the arrival of the caravan at the house.

11.8.0.en: When the dog reached the house and the mother saw it, she rejoiced and hurried to meet her son. Tobit the father, though blind, rose and ran too, forgetting his inability to see, and he kept stumbling on many things in his way, so one of the young men around him came forward to take his hand and help him to receive his son. The boy who took Tobit's hand is a type of John the Baptist, who prepared the way of Christ by his preaching and helped humanity, which was living in the darkness of sin and is typified by Tobit the father, to receive the good news of Christ, who is typified by the younger Tobias.

11.9.0.en: They went on: they remained and continued.

11.9.1.en: The meeting between Tobias and his parents was warm, and from the excess of their joy they wept. We note here that Tobias preceded his wife to his father's house, as Christ ascended to heaven to prepare a place for His Church, that she may be where He is (Jn 14:2).

11.10.0.en: Then all came forward to pray and bowed down in thanks to God, and afterward they sat and talked, and each expressed his feelings; and so they put God first before their personal talk, as we mentioned.

11.11.s.en: (2) Sight returns to Tobit the father

11.11.0.en: Tobias told his father that he had with him a medicine to treat the eyes, which he had brought with him from the journey, and asked his permission to use this medicine on him, then he rose and smeared his father's eyes with the gall of the whale (the fish). The use of the gall of the whale for healing the illness of Tobit the father was an accepted thing at that time, since medicine among the ancient Egyptians was known and used the liver, the gall and fish to anoint the sick, so that they were healed of their illnesses.

11.11.1.en: Tobias believed the angel's word that his father would be healed, yet he obeyed and smeared his eyes with the gall of the whale, and this is what happens in the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick, when the priest anoints the sick person with oil and by faith he is healed of his illnesses; for the spirit believes and the body also shares when touched with a perceptible substance.

11.11.2.en: We note that the angel specified the substance suitable for healing the illness, namely the gall, and also specified who would smear the father's eyes with the substance, namely the younger Tobias, and this is a type of the specifying of the oil of the Anointing of the Sick for healing the sick, by the hand of the priest of the New Testament.

11.12.0.en: Eggshell membrane: the thin membrane surrounding the white of a boiled egg beneath the dry shell.

11.12.1.en: Then their sitting continued in conversations of love, Tobias telling about his journey and what happened on it, and the parents telling about their circumstances. After about half an hour had passed, a thin membrane began to appear on the eyes of Tobit the father, so the younger Tobias took hold of the edge of this membrane and drew it from his father's eyes; his eyes were opened at once and he saw as he had before.

11.12.2.en: Although the healing was entirely from God by the work of His grace, we note that Tobias used a substance, the gall of the whale, and it may have been a membrane that he drew from his father's eyes. These material things were only to confirm the importance of spiritual striving in order to receive the work of divine grace. As the Lord Christ put clay on the eyes of the man born blind and asked him to wash, and as He asked those around Him to take away the stone from the door of the tomb of Lazarus (Jn 11:39), and likewise Saul of Tarsus, when he was baptized by the hand of Ananias the priest in Damascus, scales fell from his eyes and his eyes were opened (Acts 9:18). So the waiting of half an hour was to test the faith of Tobias the son and the father, for God sometimes delays His work, even for a short time, to test our faith, as takes place in the Holy Sacraments such as the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick, in which a prayer is offered for an hour and the sick person is signed with oil; besides the importance of prayer, it is an opportunity to test faith in the power of God who is able to heal.

11.12.3.en: We must complete our striving in order to receive divine grace from God who is able to do all things, and consequently our hearts should not be troubled, however hard the affliction is, or its solution seems impossible: "The things which are impossible with men are possible with God" (Lk 18:27).

11.13.0.en: There was great joy at the miraculous healing of Tobit, in which all those around him and those who knew him shared.

11.13.1.en: At once the feelings of joy turned into glorification and thanksgiving to God, and this is the conduct of the children of God which drives them to praise every day in the Church, in thanksgiving to God for His salvation, which He accomplished on the Cross and offers to them in the Church and her sacraments.

11.14.0.en: The beautiful thing is that there was not the slightest murmuring in Tobit the father, but he was accepting of the trial as a chastening from God, trusting in His mercy and the healing He had bestowed on him. Contentment and thanksgiving open the door to the work of God's grace with a person.

11.15.s.en: (3) The safe arrival of Sara and the caravan

11.15.0.en: The younger Tobias went on telling his parents all the details of the journey and all the blessings of God which He had bestowed on him by means of Azarias, his companion and guide. The parents listened with joy and longing and thanked God for His blessings.

11.15.1.en: Azarias, that is, the angel Raphael, is a type, as we mentioned, of the Holy Spirit, and through him Tobias received the many benefits of God, for the Holy Spirit is the one who gives us the blessings of salvation which Christ accomplished on the Cross.

11.15.2.en: After seven days had passed, which went by quickly as if they were moments, from the excess of joy at Tobias's meeting with his parents, Sara arrived with the servants and maidservants and all the cattle and all the money, both what she took from her parents and what they obtained from Gabael. It represents God's blessings to His children who obey His commandments. The number seven is a type of the completeness of waiting for the blessing of God, and also points to the time of the Church's (Sara's) completing her striving on earth, until she reaches heaven.

11.15.3.en: If the younger Tobias is a type of Christ who arrived at His Father's house, that is, ascended to the heavens, then Sara, who is a type of the Church, arrived after him in heaven, where He had prepared a place for her, to be with Him forever, and with her all that she acquired in the world of virtues (typified by her material possessions of servants, money and cattle), and she acquired all this because of her union with Tobias, that is, Christ, who delivered her from the captivity of Satan (Asmodeus).

11.16.0.en: Ahior: a Hebrew name meaning other.

11.16.1.en: Nabat: a Hebrew name meaning God sees.

11.16.2.en: The relatives of Tobit the father came, when they heard the news of his healing and the return of his son married and with much money, to congratulate him. The two most famous names of his relatives mentioned by the Holy Bible are Ahior (other) and Nabat (God sees), and they point to the fact that if the affliction is prolonged, God the Almighty sees everything and finally pours out His mercies and rejoices the heart of His children.

11.17.0.en: All expressed their joy with a feast that lasted seven days. The feast is a type of the feast of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of the Lord, the source of our complete joy. The number seven is a type of the completeness of joy. And if Tobit the father is a type of the Father, his relatives point to the angels, who rejoice at the arrival of the Church in heaven, after the end of this world, and live in the heavenly feast forever. And if the Church, typified by Sara, rejoiced in the house of her father Raguel with a feast, this is a type of rejoicing in Christ on earth, but in heaven also there is another joy that cannot be expressed, typified by the feast held at Tobit the father's, who is a type of the Father.
